content.title: About
content.content: Ramen bowl with chicken is a ready‑to‑cook kit that includes ramen noodles, seasoned broth, chicken pieces and aromatic spices. Simply pour hot water over the contents, add the chicken, wait a few minutes, and enjoy a flavorful, satisfying Asian‑style meal at home or at the office.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ramen originated in Japan in the early 20th century and quickly became a popular street‑food dish.
Chicken in ramen is often pre‑cooked and sliced thinly to speed up preparation.
Most instant ramen packs use dry seasonings and broth powders that preserve flavor for long periods.
Japan boasts over 10,000 ramen varieties, including chicken, pork, seafood, and vegetarian versions.
Instant ramen noodles are typically made from wheat flour, salt and water, sometimes with added starch for a smoother texture.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle repair and immune function.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Chicken and fortified broth can supply iron, important for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The kit contains B6 and B12 vitamins that support energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Carbohydrates for energy
items.content: Ramen noodles deliver quick‑acting carbs that are readily converted into energy.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: The broth often includes sodium, potassium and magnesium, which help maintain fluid and electrolyte balance.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Instant ramen packets are usually high in salt, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Additives
items.content: Flavor enhancers (MSG), preservatives and artificial aromas may be present and are not suitable for everyone.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Some kits contain gluten, soy sauce or other common allergens.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dish can be relatively calorie‑rich due to noodles and oil, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour the contents of the packet over hot (not boiling) water, stir, add the chicken pieces and let sit for 3–5 minutes. Optionally garnish with fresh vegetables, herbs, a boiled egg or a splash of soy sauce for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened packets in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the contents in an airtight container to prevent moisture absorption. Follow the expiration date printed on the packaging.
